Decode the provider's keys of a run's issues

Source: R/lineage_decode.R
gpq_decode_lineage.Rd

Shows each record-level issue in the provider's own terms: the record's source ID (src_*_id), read from tables at the issue's row, is split into the parts its contributor's lineage spec expects, and each part is labelled with the provider's table and column. The issues' provider_key, provider_key_status and fingerprint are set by reference.

Usage

gpq_decode_lineage(
  issues,
  tables,
  spec,
  key_col,
  table_map = NULL,
  flags = NULL
)

Arguments

issues

The issues table of a run's results, from gpq_check_conformance(): a data.table, changed by reference.

tables

The tables the issues came from, as gpq_check_conformance() takes them. Decoding stops if an issue's row isn't in its table or holds another primary key there.

spec

The specification the run used, from gpq_read_spec() or magp_spec().

key_col

The issues column holding each record's contributor, such as a group column of the run.

table_map

NULL, or, when tables is a DBI connection, the database's names for the specification's tables, as gpq_check_conformance() takes it.

flags

NULL, or a list named by table of data.frames, each holding the table's primary-key columns and one or more flag columns, which conditions read as flag.<name>. A record whose key the data.frame doesn't give has no flag there.

Value

issues, invisibly, with provider_key, provider_key_status and fingerprint set.

Details

A record's contributor comes from the issues' key_col value: where key_col is the last attribute of the site-ID bands' key chain, the label of that value in the bands' labels sheet, else the value itself. The ID decoded is the record's table's first ID attribute that the lineage spec gives an entry.

provider_key_status:

  • decoded: the ID split into exactly the parts the entry expects, each written as table.column=value, or for a part the pipeline derives, its attribute name and value, joined by "; ". An ID of one part isn't split.

  • partial: as decoded, but a part is blank or a missing-value code.

  • raw: the ID as delivered: it doesn't split into the expected parts (a value holding the separator), its entry has labelled alternatives, or there is no separator.

  • no_lineage_spec: the ID as delivered: the record's contributor has no entry for it.

  • fallback_pk: no key: a column-level issue, a table with no ID to decode, an ID that is missing, blank or a missing-value code, or an entry that says the contributor has no ID.

A part's label can depend on the record: the lineage spec's when conditions are tried in order before the entry's own part. A condition reads a column of the record, a parent's column through a chain of foreign keys joined by " > ", or a flag given in flags as flag.<name>.

The fingerprint becomes rule_id|table_name|column_name|<provider_key> where a key is given; where another record of the table holds the same key, and where there is no key, it stays the pk: form.

See also

gpq_check_conformance() for the issues, and gpq_classify_issues(), which classes them.

Examples

# One table of plots whose source ID is the provider's site and plot joined by "_".
dictionary <- data.frame(
  table_name = "plots",
  attribute_name = c("plot_id", "contributor", "src_plot_id", "slope"),
  key_type = c("PK", ".", ".", "."),
  data_type = c("character", "character", "character", "numeric"),
  min_value = c(NA, NA, NA, "0")
)
spec <- gpq_read_spec(
  dictionary,
  lineage_spec = data.frame(
    contributor_label = "north", table_name = "plots", attribute_name = "src_plot_id",
    spec_type = "id", source_text = "survey.site + survey.plot", note = NA,
    source_cell = NA
  ),
  lineage_separator = "_",
  id_pattern = "^src_.*_id$",
  sentinels = gpq_sentinels(numeric = c(missing = -1), character = c(missing = "X"))
)
plots <- data.frame(
  plot_id = c("p1", "p2", "p3"), contributor = "north",
  src_plot_id = c("41_2", "41_X", "41_2_b"), slope = c(-5, -6, -7)
)
results <- gpq_check_conformance(
  list(plots = plots), spec,
  group_cols = "contributor", layers = 3
)
gpq_decode_lineage(results$issues, list(plots = plots), spec, key_col = "contributor")
results$issues[, c("record_pk", "provider_key", "provider_key_status")]
#>    record_pk                  provider_key provider_key_status
#>       <char>                        <char>              <char>
#> 1:        p1 survey.site=41; survey.plot=2             decoded
#> 2:        p2 survey.site=41; survey.plot=X             partial
#> 3:        p3                        41_2_b                 raw
